evidence.excerpt:
Calibrating a cosmological simulation is an expensive, high-dimensional parameter
optimization task. Previous works employ Bayesian optimization for automation,
which treats the simulator as a black box and precludes the incorporation of
human domain knowledge or workflow into the selection policy. We propose
AGENTICTUNER, an agentic calibration pipeline with a present-day large language
model serving as the optimizer who proposes the next parameter trial. We show that
these agents can achieve competitive calibration performance at a fraction of the
CPU cost when they are given informal, human-readable priors (such as codebase,
documentation, and heuristic guides that seasoned scientists may possess). We
hope this work serves as an early step toward AI scientists that can carry out
complex, long-horizon scientific tasks. A starter code is available on GitHub.1

sequential decision process. At each step t, BO fits a probabilistic surrogate model to the trial
history Dt ={(θ τ , dτ , cτ )}τ≤t , and uses an acquisition function α(θ;D t) to propose the next point,
θt+1 = arg maxθ∈Θ α(θ;D t). The most common surrogate is a Gaussian process [GP; 20], with
tree-based and density-based alternatives also in use (e.g., TPE [ 5], SMAC [15]). Regardless of
surrogate choice, BO treats the optimization process as a black box with a non-informative prior,
which prevents the integration of domain-specific knowledge or workflow into the selection policy.

Loop design.AGENTICTUNERis an agentic simulation calibration system that replaces an acquisi-
tion function with an LLM as the optimizer (see Figure 1). The central loop of AGENTICTUNERis
orchestrated by the external harness, which is separate from and independent of the LLM. Each
iteration t begins with the instantiation of a stateless LLM instance within a sandboxed container that
conceals the hidden ground truth θtrue. Because LLM performance has been shown to deteriorate
with a monotonically increasing context window [8, 27, 26], we opt to clear the context [3] after the
LLM calls an expensive simulator for the proposed trial θt+1. When the simulation is finished, the
harness mediates the evaluation process by calculating ˜χ2(θt+1) and either restarting the loop with a
fresh agent or stopping the search if˜χ2 <1or a fixed CPU-hour budget is exhausted.

Anatomy of reasoning.To gain insight into the LLM's decision-making process while tackling a
long-horizon task, we examine the lab notebook and reasoning trace during the first and last half of
each run's invocations (see Figure 3). The LLM begins each new invocation with no memory other
than what is written to disk, necessitating a fixed reorientation cost (about 30% of the budget) by
scanning the workspace files. During the early stages, the agent focuses on calling cheap PROBE
proxies (7%) and doing residual analysis (6%), initially to localize the cosmological parameters and

evidence.excerpt:
In this work, we present AGENTICTUNER, an agentic calibration system that uses an LLM agent
to propose the parameter point based on trial history and human-authored priors. We evaluate our
system in calibrating a costly cosmological simulation and find that AGENTICTUNERoutperforms
the Bayesian optimization baseline in simulation cost across all runs. Auditing the reasoning trace
of the LLM agent demonstrates its ability to adapt the search strategy during a run from active tool
use to synthesizing previous findings. These results suggest that natural-language priors significantly
improve the selection process.

context components (guide, codebase, low-resolution probe) to isolate what drives sample efficiency.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The headline sample-efficiency gain is measured by the external harness's numerical reduced chi-squared on forward simulator outputs, which is not the signal used to shape the agent's proposals.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Convergence is established by an objective reduced chi-squared statistic computed by the external harness from forward MP-Gadget simulation power spectra against the target spectrum.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The LLM agent's parameter proposals are shaped by natural-language heuristic guides, simulator documentation, trial history, and low-fidelity CAMB proxy queries.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: The experimental evidence directly supports the claim of reduced computational expense and sample efficiency on the evaluated MP-Gadget 12-parameter calibration task under the provided guide and tool setup.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation across 20 synthetic cosmological calibration runs demonstrates that AGENTICTUNER reaches convergence (reduced chi-squared < 1 against target matter power spectra) using a median of 8.5 high-resolution simulation calls, compared to 17.5 for standard Gaussian process Bayesian optimization.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Convergence and trial efficiency are established by objective numerical chi-squared calculation executed by the external harness on forward MP-Gadget simulation outputs.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Objective reduced chi-squared statistical goodness-of-fit computed from forward MP-Gadget simulation matter power spectra against target data.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Heuristic prompting, trial history logs, and low-resolution CAMB proxy simulator runs guided by natural language documentation.

primary.limitations: The authors acknowledge that testing is limited to a single simulator setup and matter power spectrum observable, and that formal ablations isolating the exact contribution of each workspace component (e.g., guide vs proxy) remain future work.
primary.method_assessment: The system design isolates the LLM across iterative runs by clearing context and persisting knowledge via an append-only workspace, preventing memory bloat while incorporating domain documentation and cheap proxy simulations to guide parameter choices.
primary.quality_rationale: The study presents a clear, well-scoped methodology with an objective, simulator-derived quantitative metric (reduced chi-squared based on cosmic variance). The experimental protocol includes baseline comparisons, confidence intervals across 20 runs, and detailed documentation in the appendix.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces AGENTICTUNER, a framework that uses an LLM agent equipped with structured natural language physical priors, simulator code, and a low-fidelity CAMB proxy tool to calibrate parameters in high-dimensional cosmological hydrodynamic simulations.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study presents a clear, well-scoped methodology with an objective, simulator-derived quantitative metric (reduced chi-squared based on cosmic variance). The experimental protocol includes baseline comparisons, confidence intervals across 20 runs, and detailed documentation in the appendix.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors acknowledge that testing is limited to a single simulator setup and matter power spectrum observable, and that formal ablations isolating the exact contribution of each workspace component (e.g., guide vs proxy) remain future work.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.

research_relevance.value: Directly relevant to autonomous/deep research workflows based on screening evidence.
